Artificial Intelligence words are seen in this illustration taken March 31, 2023. REUTERS/Dado Ruvic/Illustration/File Photo

High levels of borrowing to fund artificial intelligence infrastructure is expanding private credit beyond traditional corporate lending, but a wave of loans coming due in the next few years could leave weaker borrowers struggling to refinance, Moody's Ratings said on Tuesday.

The ratings agency said AI financing needs now extend beyond data-center construction to land, power, semiconductors, graphics processing units and tensor processing units

Moody's expects capital spending by the five largest US hyperscalers and CoreWeave to reach nearly US$1 trillion (HK$7.8 trillion) in 2027, financed through cash flows, debt and structures such as joint ventures and special-purpose vehicles

However, a wave of loans coming due between 2027 and 2029 will test weaker borrowers’ ability to refinance at higher interest rates, Moody’s said

About 17 percent of the 607 borrowers tracked by Moody’s used payment-in-kind interest, which allows companies to defer cash interest payments but adds to their debt burden

A Reuters analysis earlier this year found loan maturities at US business development companies would peak in 2028 and 2029

Recent stress in CoreWeave debt has also highlighted investors’ growing concerns about highly leveraged AI borrowers
